newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran helicopter crashes in Gulf war games.
newsitem.headline: Iran helicopter crashes in Gulf war games.

text.p: An Iranian helicopter crashed in the Gulf late on Wednesday during a major military exercise, Iran's state-run television said on Thursday.
The crash occurred during troop movement manoeuvres and was the result of technical failure, said the television, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC).
The report did not say whether anyone was killed or injured.
Some 100 ships, including destroyers, gunboats, hovercraft and Iran's two Russian-built submarines were taking part in the exercise, backed by 40 planes and helicopters.
Tehran radio earlier said Iranian forces landed from air and sea on an island in the war games near the mouth of the Gulf on Thursday to defeat occupying "enemy troops".
It said navy forces, backed by intensive fire from air force planes and naval vessels, landed on the island and were joined by paratroopers from the army and the Revolutionary Guards.
The forces defeated the mock enemy in the manoeuvres held in a 2,000-square-km (770-square-mile) area, the radio added.

Britain and the United Arab Emirates on Thursday signed a defence cooperation accord which pledged British help to deter aggression if the oil-rich Gulf state, nervous about an Iranian arms buildup, is threatened.
Tehran, which is engaged in a dispute with the UAE over sovereignty of three strategic Gulf islands, says its military programme is purely defensive.
Western naval sources on Tuesday confirmed an Iranian report that Iran, the only Gulf state with submarines, would soon receive a third Russian diesel submarine.
